meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Cai G, Zhang L, Zhang Y, Zhang J, Zhou J et al.
articles.title: Effects of a Nurse-Led Multicomponent Exercise Intervention for Haemodialysis Patients With Possible or Confirmed Sarcopenia: A Cluster Randomised Trial.
articles.summary: A cluster randomized trial evaluating a 12-week nurse-led multicomponent exercise program for hemodialysis patients with sarcopenia.

pico.population: Hemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia (n=56)
pico.intervention: 12-week nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention plus standard care
pico.outcome: Skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), handgrip strength, gait speed, and Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores

appraisal.bottom_line: The 12-week nurse-led exercise intervention showed favorable trends in muscle strength and physical function with moderate-to-large effect sizes, but no primary outcomes reached statistical significance after Bonferroni correction.
appraisal.relevance: Sarcopenia is a major contributor to morbidity in dialysis; while this nurse-led model is feasible and safe, its efficacy remains unproven in this small cohort.
appraisal.caveat: The study was likely underpowered (n=56) to detect differences after adjusting for multiple comparisons, and the cluster design may introduce bias if not properly accounted for.

articles.authors: Brashear SE, Mohamed Sulthan A, Chan D, Rao V, Begue G et al.
articles.title: Skeletal muscle adaptation to home-based exercise in chronic kidney disease.
articles.summary: A randomized trial examining skeletal muscle biopsies before and after a 12-week home-based exercise program in patients with CKD stages 3-5.

pico.intervention: 12-week home-based, video-monitored exercise program (HIIT, power walking, and strength training)
pico.outcome: Muscle fiber size, satellite cell count, capillarization, and fibroadipogenic progenitors

appraisal.bottom_line: A 12-week home-based exercise program increased muscle capillarization and decreased fibroadipogenic progenitors, although it did not significantly alter muscle fiber size or satellite cell numbers.
appraisal.relevance: Demonstrates that even home-based, endurance-focused exercise can induce favorable physiological remodeling in the skeletal muscle of CKD patients.
appraisal.caveat: The sample size was very small (n=25 total, with only 6 in the control group), limiting the generalizability and statistical power of the findings.

articles.title: Rethinking glycemic monitoring: a HTA of glycated albumin for type 2 diabetes with stage IV-V CKD.
articles.summary: A Health Technology Assessment (HTA) evaluating the clinical and economic impact of using glycated albumin (GA) versus HbA1c in patients with T2DM and advanced CKD.

pico.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes and stage IV-V CKD
pico.outcome: Accuracy of identifying poor glycemic control, adverse events, and cost-effectiveness

appraisal.bottom_line: Glycated albumin identified poor glycemic control more accurately than HbA1c (52% vs. 19.2%) and was estimated to be cost-saving (2.02% annual saving) for the Italian healthcare system.
appraisal.relevance: HbA1c is often unreliable in advanced CKD due to altered red cell turnover; GA provides a more accurate glycemic marker in this specific population.
appraisal.caveat: The study is a Health Technology Assessment combining a systematic review with economic modeling and stakeholder surveys, rather than a primary clinical trial.

articles.authors: Nishiwaki H, Levack WM, Hasegawa T, Ota E, Noma H et al.
articles.title: Music-based interventions for people with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis.
articles.summary: A Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 RCTs assessing music-based interventions for symptom burden in hemodialysis patients.

pico.population: Patients with kidney failure undergoing hemodialysis
pico.comparison: Usual care, headphones without music, or video
pico.outcome: Fatigue, blood pressure, depression, and pain

inclusion: Participants with kidney failure undergoing hemodialysis
exclusion: Temporary hemodialysis for acute kidney injury

appraisal.bottom_line: Music-based interventions may reduce short-term fatigue (MD -3.14, 95% CI -3.83 to -2.45), depressive symptoms (SMD -0.88, 95% CI -1.51 to -0.25), and pain (SMD -0.89, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.15), though the certainty of evidence is low.
appraisal.relevance: Music offers a low-cost, non-pharmacological adjunct to manage the high symptom burden associated with maintenance dialysis.
appraisal.caveat: High heterogeneity (I² up to 92%) and low-to-very-low certainty of evidence across outcomes; long-term effects remain unknown.

articles.authors: Gao J, Wang J, Wang Z
articles.title: Association of remnant cholesterol with kidney outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies exploring the association between remnant cholesterol (RC) and kidney outcomes in type 2 diabetes.

pico.outcome: Incident diabetic kidney disease (DKD), kidney failure, and DKD progression

exclusion: Mixed populations where T2DM-specific data could not be extracted

appraisal.bottom_line: Higher remnant cholesterol is associated with incident DKD (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17-1.37), but the association with kidney failure did not reach statistical significance (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.82-2.97).
appraisal.relevance: RC may serve as a complementary lipid marker for kidney risk in diabetic patients beyond traditional LDL-C measurements.
appraisal.caveat: The evidence is purely observational and cannot establish causality; significant heterogeneity was noted in the overall analysis (I² = 87.6%).

articles.authors: Zhang J, Chen X, Yao L, Li T, Sun X et al.
articles.title: Crystalline κ-light-chain proximal tubulopathy in Waldenström macroglobulinemia with an IgA nephropathy pattern: a case report and systematic review.
articles.summary: A case report and systematic review of crystalline κ-light-chain proximal tubulopathy (LCPT) in Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM).

pico.population: Patients with Waldenström macroglobulinemia and LCPT or crystal-storing histiocytosis

appraisal.bottom_line: Crystalline κ-LCPT is a rare renal manifestation of WM that can be successfully managed with BTK inhibitors, leading to stable renal function and sustained hematological response.
appraisal.relevance: Nephrologists should consider LCPT in WM patients with proteinuria and dysfunction, as targeted hematological therapy can preserve kidney function.
appraisal.caveat: The systematic review identified only 7 prior cases, making the evidence base extremely limited and subject to publication bias.

articles.authors: Chen S, Wu M, Huang M, Lu B, Wang J et al.
articles.title: Baseline gut microbiota and short-term response to acupressure combined with thermal stimulation in maintenance hemodialysis patients with functional constipation: an exploratory responder analysis.
articles.summary: An exploratory responder analysis of a crossover trial investigating if baseline gut microbiota predicts response to acupressure and thermal stimulation for constipation in HD patients.

pico.population: Maintenance hemodialysis patients with functional constipation (n=26)
pico.outcome: Baseline gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing)

appraisal.bottom_line: While Veillonella and Lactobacillus showed nominal associations with treatment response, no baseline microbial characteristics were robustly predictive of response to acupressure and thermal stimulation.
appraisal.relevance: The gut-kidney axis may influence symptom management, but current microbial profiling is not yet ready for clinical use in predicting intervention success.
appraisal.caveat: Small sample size (n=26) and the exploratory, post-hoc nature of the responder analysis limit the reliability of the findings.

articles.authors: Walter-Cano S, Lee A, Andrade JM
articles.title: Effectiveness of mHealth Nutrition Interventions on Nutrition-Related and Clinical Outcomes in Adults with Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 studies evaluating mHealth nutrition interventions in adults with CKD.

pico.outcome: Biochemical outcomes, interdialytic weight gain, and dietary intake

appraisal.bottom_line: Meta-analysis of randomized trials found no significant effect of mHealth interventions on biochemical outcomes or interdialytic weight gain in dialysis patients.
appraisal.relevance: Despite the proliferation of health apps, high-quality evidence supporting their clinical efficacy in improving hard nutritional or clinical outcomes in CKD is currently lacking.
appraisal.caveat: Most positive findings were derived from pre-post studies without control groups, which are prone to temporal bias and cannot establish intervention efficacy.

articles.authors: Hu J, Pan X, Wei S, Wei J
articles.title: Prognostic value of multiple biomarkers for kidney function decline in type 2 diabetes with relatively preserved kidney function: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies evaluating biomarkers for kidney function decline in early DKD.

pico.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes and relatively preserved kidney function
pico.intervention: Baseline circulating or urinary biomarkers (e.g., TNFR1, TNFR2, KIM-1)

inclusion: Type 2 diabetes with relatively preserved kidney function

appraisal.bottom_line: Circulating TNFR1, TNFR2, and KIM-1 show potential associations with kidney function decline in early DKD, but evidence is currently too heterogeneous for definitive quantitative pooling.
appraisal.relevance: Identifying patients at high risk for progression when GFR is still preserved is critical for early intensive intervention.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis is exploratory; most pooled estimates were based on only two studies with varying definitions of kidney decline.

articles.authors: Mozafar M, Bigdeli Y, Lichani MA, Looha MA, Mozafar M et al.
articles.title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 139 cases of infectious arterial complications in kidney transplant recipients to evaluate vascular management strategies.

pico.population: Kidney transplant recipients with culture-proven infectious vascular complications
pico.intervention: Various vascular management strategies (e.g., autologous grafting, stenting, ligation)
pico.outcome: Uneventful recovery, reintervention, mortality, and limb loss

appraisal.bottom_line: Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery), while arterial ligation was associated with the highest mortality (43.8%).
appraisal.relevance: Provides a clinical framework for managing rare but catastrophic infectious vascular events in transplant recipients, favoring autologous reconstruction over ligation.
appraisal.caveat: The review is based on case reports spanning 50 years, which are subject to significant reporting bias and lack of standardized management protocols.

articles.authors: Sotiriou G, Karava V, Dotis J
articles.title: Thyroid Dysfunction in Children with Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies estimating the prevalence of subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) in children with CKD.
inclusion: CKD stages 1-5 including kidney replacement therapy

appraisal.bottom_line: The pooled prevalence of subclinical hypothyroidism in children with CKD is 12.8% (95% CI, 9.2-17.6%), with no detected heterogeneity among peer-reviewed studies.
appraisal.relevance: Thyroid dysfunction is common in pediatric CKD, but the clinical significance and benefit of levothyroxine therapy in this population remain unproven.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis is based on a small number of studies (n=7) and participants (n=403), and definitions of SCH varied across the included literature.

articles.authors: Guo M, Han X, Xu X
articles.title: Meta-analysis of the effectiveness of nursing interventions in the care of adult patients with kidney failure.
articles.summary: A broad systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 studies evaluating the impact of various nursing interventions on outcomes in kidney failure.

pico.intervention: Nursing interventions (shared-care, education, music therapy, etc.)

appraisal.bottom_line: Nursing interventions significantly increased patient satisfaction (MD 2.71, 95% CI 1.72-3.70) and reduced complication rates (MD -7.39, 95% CI -11.48 to -3.31) compared to control groups.
appraisal.relevance: Underscores the critical role of specialized nursing care in improving patient-centered outcomes in the dialysis and CKD population.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis pools extremely diverse interventions (from music therapy to shared-care models), making the aggregate effect size difficult to apply to any single specific nursing practice.
